details.answerQuote: Binomial expression is usually of the form (a + b)ⁿ where a, b are algebraic terms and n is a real number.
sectionParagraphs: A binomial expression is usually of the form (a + b)ⁿ where a, b are algebraic terms and n is a real number. If n is a natural number, one may decide to expand the bracket by multiplying two brackets then use the result to multiply another bracket until the power of n is exhausted. This approach could be time consuming in a case of large value of n and the approach may never work when n is not a natural number. In this lesson, we present the approaches to expanding binomial expression for any value of n in the set of real numbers.
sectionSteps: Recognize that binomial expressions have the form (a + b)ⁿ with algebraic terms a, b and real number n.
Understand that repeated bracket multiplication works for natural number powers but is time consuming for large n.
Note that the repeated multiplication approach may never work when n is not a natural number.
Learn the general approaches for expanding binomial expressions for any real number n.

details.answerQuote: (a + b)ⁿ equals the sum from k=0 to n of (n choose k) times aⁿ⁻ᵏ times bᵏ.
sectionParagraphs: A binomial expression of the form (a + b)ⁿ, n ∈ ℕ can be expanded using a formula. The formula shows the expansion as a sum of terms involving binomial coefficients and powers of a and b.
sectionSteps: Identify the binomial expression (a + b)ⁿ where n is a natural number.
Apply the formula: (a + b)ⁿ equals the sum from k=0 to n of (n choose k) times aⁿ⁻ᵏ times bᵏ.
The first term is (n choose 0) aⁿ b⁰, the second is (n choose 1) aⁿ⁻¹ b¹, continuing to the last term (n choose n) a⁰ bⁿ.

sectionParagraphs: This page defines the binomial coefficient (n choose m) as n! divided by (n−m)! times m!, and n! as n × (n−1) × (n−2) × ⋯ × 2 × 1. The page then calculates each binomial coefficient for n = 5: (5 choose 0) = 1, (5 choose 1) = 5, (5 choose 2) = 10, (5 choose 3) = 10, (5 choose 4) = 5, and (5 choose 5) = 1. Each calculation shows the factorial expansions and simplifications step by step.
sectionSteps: Define (n choose m) = n! / [(n−m)! m!] and n! = n × (n−1) × (n−2) × ⋯ × 2 × 1.
Calculate (5 choose 0) = 5! / (5! · 0!) = 1.
Calculate (5 choose 1) = 5! / (4! · 1!) = 5.
Calculate (5 choose 2) = 5! / (3! · 2!) = 10.
Calculate (5 choose 3) = 5! / (2! · 3!) = 10.
Calculate (5 choose 4) = 5! / (1! · 4!) = 5 and (5 choose 5) = 1.

details.answerQuote: In cases where the power n of a given binomial expression is negative or fraction, we transform the binomial expression into the form (1 − x)ⁿ then use the formula: (1 − x)ⁿ = 1 − nx + [n(n−1)/2!]x² − [n(n−1)(n−2)/3!]x³ + ⋯.
sectionParagraphs: In cases where the power n of a given binomial expression is negative or fraction, we transform the binomial expression into the form (1 − x)ⁿ then use the formula: (1 − x)ⁿ = 1 − nx + [n(n−1)/2!]x² − [n(n−1)(n−2)/3!]x³ + ⋯. An example is given: Find the binomial expansion of (1 + 3x)⁻⁴ to the fourth term.
sectionSteps: Recognize that for negative or fractional n, transform the expression into the form (1 − x)ⁿ.
Apply the formula: (1 − x)ⁿ = 1 − nx + [n(n−1)/2!]x² − [n(n−1)(n−2)/3!]x³ + ⋯.
Use this formula to expand (1 + 3x)⁻⁴ to the fourth term.
